proposals.statement:
theorem damage_front_advances (X Y : Config) (t k : ℕ)
    (hagree : ∀ i ≤ k + 1, column X (-(i : ℤ)) t = column Y (-(i : ℤ)) t)
    (hdiff : column X (-((k : ℤ) + 2)) t ≠ column Y (-((k : ℤ) + 2)) t) :
    (∀ i, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ k → column X (-(i : ℤ)) (t + 1) = column Y (-(i : ℤ)) (t + 1))
      ∧ column X (-((k : ℤ) + 1)) (t + 1) ≠ column Y (-((k : ℤ) + 1)) (t + 1) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: Two pictures agree on a clean block of cells running left from the origin to depth k+1, and differ at depth k+2. One step later the disagreement stands exactly one place nearer the origin, and the block behind it is still clean. Each cell at depth i with 1 ≤ i ≤ k reads depths i-1, i, i+1 a step earlier, all inside the agreeing block, so it agrees; the cell at depth k+1 reads depth k+2, which differs, and depths k+1 and k, which agree, and rule 30 is XOR with the left neighbour, so its two values differ. Depth 0 is deliberately not claimed: it reads position +1, about which nothing is assumed. This is the finite-window twin of the closed rightmost_difference_moves_right, which needs agreement at EVERY position to the right and so does not apply here — P1's residual is exactly the case where the right half carries damage and only a finite stretch beside the origin is clean. It is the step lemma the arrival statement below iterates.
proposals.disclaims: Nothing about the centre column, nothing about periodicity, nothing about rule 30 beyond one application of rule30_eq. Band: Nothing — a one-step statement true of the picture grown from any two rows. Its value is entirely as the iterable form the other nodes need.

route.tactics:
have hstep : ∀ (Z : Config) (j : ℤ),
      column Z j (t + 1)
        = xor (column Z (j - 1) t) (column Z j t || column Z (j + 1) t) := by
    intro Z j
    show evolveFrom Z (t + 1) j = _
    rw [evolveFrom_succ, rule30_eq]
    rfl
  have bxor : ∀ a a' b : Bool, xor a b = xor a' b → a = a' := by decide
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i hi1 hik
    have h1 : column X (-(i : ℤ) - 1) t = column Y (-(i : ℤ) - 1) t := by
      have e : -(i : ℤ) - 1 = -((i + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by omega
      rw [e]; exact hagree (i + 1) (by omega)
    have h2 : column X (-(i : ℤ)) t = column Y (-(i : ℤ)) t := hagree i (by omega)
    have h3 : column X (-(i : ℤ) + 1) t = column Y (-(i : ℤ) + 1) t := by
      have e : -(i : ℤ) + 1 = -((i - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by omega
      rw [e]; exact hagree (i - 1) (by omega)
    rw [hstep X, hstep Y, h1, h2, h3]
  · have h1 : column X (-((k : ℤ) + 1) - 1) t ≠ column Y (-((k : ℤ) + 1) - 1) t := by
      have e : -((k : ℤ) + 1) - 1 = -((k : ℤ) + 2) := by omega
      rw [e]; exact hdiff
    have h2 : column X (-((k : ℤ) + 1)) t = column Y (-((k : ℤ) + 1)) t := by
      have e : -((k : ℤ) + 1) = -((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by omega
      rw [e]; exact hagree (k + 1) (by omega)
    have h3 : column X (-((k : ℤ) + 1) + 1) t = column Y (-((k : ℤ) + 1) + 1) t := by
      have e : -((k : ℤ) + 1) + 1 = -((k : ℕ) : ℤ) := by omega
      rw [e]; exact hagree k (by omega)
    rw [hstep X, hstep Y, h2, h3]
    exact fun hEq => h1 (bxor _ _ _ hEq)

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_damage_front_exists (p t : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p)
    (h0 : evolve t 0 = evolve (t + p) 0) :
    ∃ k, (∀ i ≤ k, evolve t (-(i : ℤ)) = evolve (t + p) (-(i : ℤ)))
      ∧ evolve t (-((k : ℤ) + 1)) ≠ evolve (t + p) (-((k : ℤ) + 1)) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: Compare the picture with itself slid forward by p — the one pair of pictures the prize is about, since a centre column of period p is exactly the statement that this pair agrees at the origin from some time on. The two always differ somewhere left of the origin: at depth t + p the unslid picture is outside its own cone and therefore white (evolve_eq_false_of_outside_cone, since t < t + p), while the slid picture is sitting on its black left edge (evolve_left_edge). So the set of differing depths is non-empty, its least element exists, and that element is at least 1 because depth 0 agrees by hypothesis; writing it as k + 1 is the statement. What it buys: the damage front the next two nodes describe is not a hypothetical object introduced to make a conditional look sharp — it is there at every single time, so the arrival lemma below fires at every time rather than only where a prover can point.
proposals.disclaims: The hypothesis h0 is an instance of the counterfactual periodicity assumption; nobody can exhibit a t at which it is interesting. Band: Nothing — a least-element argument over two closed cone facts. It proves only that the front exists, never how deep it is.

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_periodic_damage_mask (p N : ℕ)
    (hc : ∀ t ≥ N, centerColumn (t + p) = centerColumn t) (t : ℕ) (ht : N ≤ t) :
    xor (evolve t (-1)) (evolve (t + p) (-1))
      = ((! centerColumn t) && xor (evolve t 1) (evolve (t + p) 1)) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The closed column_neg_one_damage_mask, read on the pair the prize is about: X the picture, Y the picture slid forward by p. evolveFrom_evolve (closed) says the picture grown from row p is the picture from time p on, so column (evolve p) i t is evolve (t + p) i, and the two hypotheses that lemma needs — the two centre columns agreeing at t and at t + 1 — are exactly the assumed period read at t and at t + 1, both of which are at least N. The content is that the residual of P1 is ONE object rather than two: under a periodic centre column, the failure of column -1 to repeat at time t is the very same Bool as the failure of column +1, gated on the centre cell being white. It recovers the closed centerColumn_periodic_neg_one_black_times as the black case of a single identity, and it is what turns a statement about the incoming left damage into a statement about column 1, which is where the board's four sufficient conditions live. Checked over 605 qualifying instances at p ≤ 12 against a direct cell-by-cell rule 30 (explorer/seeder13_damage.mjs), 0 failures.
proposals.disclaims: Does not prove P1 and does not weaken it. The hypothesis is eventual periodicity, which is the negation of the prize, so the identity describes a world nobody can exhibit. It is not a fifth sufficient condition — it is an identity, and it says nothing about whether the two failures can be arranged to occur together, which is the whole residual.

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_periodic_damage_arrival (p N : ℕ)
    (hc : ∀ t ≥ N, centerColumn (t + p) = centerColumn t) (t k : ℕ) (ht : N ≤ t)
    (hagree : ∀ i ≤ k, evolve t (-(i : ℤ)) = evolve (t + p) (-(i : ℤ)))
    (hdiff : evolve t (-((k : ℤ) + 1)) ≠ evolve (t + p) (-((k : ℤ) + 1))) :
    centerColumn (t + k) = false ∧ evolve (t + k) 1 ≠ evolve (t + k + p) 1 := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The capstone of the tier, and the one node here with content. Under a periodic centre column the picture and its own slide by p agree at the origin at every time from N on, which is precisely the extra fact damage_front_advances needs in order to be iterated: that lemma re-establishes cleanliness only at depths 1 and beyond, and periodicity supplies depth 0 for free. So the front cannot stall and cannot retreat — it marches exactly one place towards the origin per row, and from depth k + 1 at time t it stands at depth 1 at time t + k. There the mask identity applies and forces two things at once: the centre cell at t + k is white, and column +1 fails to repeat at that same moment. Read as a mechanism: the slid picture has a left cone p cells wider than the unslid one, so damage is being fed in from the left at every time; a periodic centre column is the claim that all of it can be walked to the origin and paid off, arrival by arrival, by a white centre cell with a matching failure on the right. That is what a proof of the prize has to contradict, and the board has never stated it. Checked over 193 qualifying instances at p ≤ 12 against a direct cell-by-cell rule 30 (explorer/seeder13_damage.mjs), 0 failures; the mutant that claims the front stays put instead of advancing fails 151 of 307 times on the same data, so the check has teeth.
proposals.disclaims: Band: project-internal. It does NOT prove P1, and it is not a sufficient condition for it: the hypothesis is eventual periodicity, so this describes what a periodic centre column would have to arrange, not that it cannot. Two specific things it does not give. It says nothing about the SUPPLY of damage — how deep the front is at each time, hence how often arrivals happen — and the counting of arrivals against the available white times is where a contradiction would have to come from. And it is a statement about the left half only; the compensating failure at column +1 is asserted, not explained, and explaining it is obstruction 9. Note also that the ≤ p spacing of white times that would make an arrival count bite is itself only available from the counterfactual run bounds, not from the picture.

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_black_run_le_period (p N : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p)
    (hc : ∀ t ≥ N, centerColumn (t + p) = centerColumn t)
    (t : ℕ) (ht : N ≤ t) (hrun : ∀ s < p, centerColumn (t + s) = true) :
    False := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The black twin of the closed centerColumn_white_run_le_period, with the same proof: p consecutive black centre cells at a time past the onset, plus the period p, make every later cell black by strong induction on how far past the run's start it sits, and centerColumn_not_eventually_constant says the centre column is white arbitrarily late. Why it is wanted rather than merely true: the white version alone gives the one-sided bound that crystal 73 reads as a finite alphabet, and the two together give the two-sided one — under a period p, every maximal run of the centre column, of either colour, is shorter than p, so the trace over one period is a bounded composition of bounded runs of both colours. It is also exactly the missing half of the p = 2 rung below, where the white bound kills the block 00 and this kills 11.
proposals.disclaims: Band: Nothing. It mirrors a closed node line for line and adds no rule 30 content of its own; its hypothesis is counterfactual, so like the white version it bounds the alphabet of an object nobody can construct. Seeded as supply for the rung below and for crystal 73's alphabet reading, not as progress.

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_periodic_two_alternating (N : ℕ)
    (hc : ∀ t ≥ N, centerColumn (t + 2) = centerColumn t) (t : ℕ) (ht : N ≤ t) :
    centerColumn (t + 1) = ! centerColumn t := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: Prize 1 is the statement that no period works, and the board holds exactly one instance of it: p = 1, which is centerColumn_not_eventually_constant, closed at opus for $2.13. This is the reduction of the next rung. If the centre column had period 2 from N and two adjacent cells past N were equal, that is a run of length 2, which is a run of length p; the closed white bound forbids it when both are white and the black twin above forbids it when both are black. So a period-2 centre column is an alternating one, and the p = 2 instance of Prize 1 is exactly the statement that the centre column is not eventually alternating — equivalently that the block 00 or the block 11 occurs arbitrarily late. That passes the measurement clause of the P1 fence: whether a given block recurs is something a script can look for at depth, where 'is it aperiodic' is not, and both blocks are seen constantly in the seed. Reached independently by Ephemeris (docs/attacks, 2026-09-12) from the subshift side, where it is the open half of the occurrence ladder's second rung; the derivation here is different and shorter, going through the two run bounds rather than through parity.
proposals.disclaims: It does NOT prove the p = 2 instance — it reduces it, and the reduction is the cheap half. The instance itself is open: an alternating tail is not refutable by anything on the board, because it propagates leftward without closing (columns -1 and -2 are pinned to a single free bit per pair, and the cone boundary is never reached — the run bounds put the forced block at depth below the time, which is crystal 69's ratio again). And the ladder does not obviously continue: this argument is special to p = 2, where a repeated adjacent pair IS a run of length p, and gives nothing at p ≥ 3.
